A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KramaBench and DS-Guru. All 23 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison of text, figures, tables and equations despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of DS-Guru configurations and proprietary systems, including benchmark scores, automation-level comparisons and runtimes in Tables 4–6.

after.justification: V2 retains original evaluations and adds smolagents comparisons, oracle-input experiments, obscured-input tests, sensitivity studies and failure analyses.

M1.justification: V1's naive, simple-planning and self-correcting variants correspond to v2's no-context, one-shot and few-shot variants. Sampling, task decomposition, Python execution and iterative error feedback are retained, and the appendix system prompt is unchanged. The newly named One-Pass Sampling mechanism does not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: The underlying coverage remains 104 tasks, 633 subtasks, six domains and 1,764 files. V2 adds gold-file-only scenarios that remove discovery requirements and obscured-input scenarios covering about 20% of tasks from legal and wildfire domains. These extend tested input conditions within the existing task structures and domains.

E2.justification: V2 adds smolagents Deep Research with GPT-o3, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5 and Claude-3.7, introducing a substantial agentic comparator alongside DS-Guru. OpenAI Deep Research and Gemini remain in the trimmed-input comparison. The additional OpenAI Deep Research entry in v1 Table 4 is omitted from the corresponding overall table.

E3.justification: V2 introduces oracle controls, obscured-input evaluation, sampling sweeps of 10–150 rows and iteration-budget sweeps of 5–20. It also revises the stated task-validation workflow from two independent reconstructions to a second solver plus a third adjudicator; this does not establish that validation was rerun. Primary scoring remains unchanged, while v1 Table 8's supplementary BLEU/ROUGE and other metric evaluations disappear.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's automation-level comparisons and brief qualitative observations, v2 adds retrieval controls, sample-size and iteration sensitivity studies, and obscured-data tests of reliance on prior knowledge. Section 4.2 adds two environmental case studies and trace-based diagnosis of failures to resolve data conventions. These substantially expand investigation of failure mechanisms.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for benchmark performance. V2's additional mean token costs and iteration-budget experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting or repeated-run estimation.

E6.justification: All 126 original domain-level DS-Guru scores and 54 lower-automation scores are retained. New smolagents/Claude-3.7 results report 50% under Full, 59% under Oracle and 57.85% under Trimmed inputs; these are added comparisons, not improvements to an unchanged configuration. V2 also adds obscured-input, sensitivity and failure-frequency results, while removing v1's partially populated Table 8 and its separate 8.47% OpenAI Deep Research entry.

T1.justification: The end-to-end averaging formula, functionality-coverage score and six answer-type scoring schemes are retained. Detailed equations move from v1 Section 3 to v2 Appendix E. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: V1 primarily introduces the benchmark and DS-Guru and argues that existing systems struggle with end-to-end pipelines. V2 adds central claims about the benefits of agentic control flow, persistent failures with oracle retrieval, and limitations in data-dependent reasoning and prior-knowledge integration. Its abstract foregrounds the 50% full-input and 59% oracle-input results, while DS-Guru is positioned as minimal reference scaffolding.

C2.justification: V2 develops explanations involving coupled retrieval and pipeline revision, competing helpful and harmful effects of prior knowledge, and failures to infer conventions across a data lake. These substantially extend v1's speculation about wildfire memorization and debugging limitations. V2 also adds discussion of language, cultural and domain-coverage limitations and biomedical re-identification risks.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents GPT-o3's role in functionality annotation, fallback to no snippets when context limits are exceeded, evaluation token costs, and curation/reproduction scripts. It also explains source-only distribution for redistribution-restricted datasets. Existing dataset-source descriptions, the system prompt and the public repository disclosure are largely retained.

R1.justification: The QA discussion replaces examples such as QASPER, HotpotQA and MMQA with agentic retrieval benchmarks including FanOutQA, CRAG and BrowseComp. V2 adds agent-system and failure-analysis references and drops v1's explicit first-benchmark claim. The central positioning against existing data-science benchmarks and the substantive comparisons in Table 1 remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and much of the explanatory narrative are rewritten. Benchmark design, evaluation and reference implementation are consolidated into Section 2; setup and results are reorganized, and appendices are reordered. V1's unfinished evaluation-mode appendix is replaced with established evaluation descriptions, and ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, and Figure 2 adds illustrated environmental case data. Results are reorganized into Full/Oracle/Trimmed displays, with new mechanism-comparison and ablation tables and extended results in Appendix A. V1's partially populated final table is removed, and appendix prompts receive boxed formatting.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens benchmark validation through a capable agentic comparator, oracle controls, obscured-input tests and concrete failure analyses, addressing v1's largely untested explanations of retrieval and memorization failures. Reorganization also removes the unfinished evaluation appendix. Some new interpretations remain unreliable—for example, Table 12 falls from 23.36% at five iterations to 21.33% at twenty despite prose claiming improvement—and uncertainty reporting remains absent. These limitations temper individual conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial gains in diagnostic evidence and clarity.
